text:
Match each type of AI technology (1-4) with its CORRECT description (A-D):
1. Symbolic AI
2. Classical machine learning
3. Deep learning
4. Generative AI
A. Uses neural networks to automatically learn features from data.
B. Uses rule-based systems to mimic human decision-making.
C. Uses deep learning to create new data by learning from its training data.
D. Uses a data-driven approach that requires feature selection.
explanation: Symbolic AI is rule-based (B). Classical ML is data-driven and needs manual feature selection (D). Deep learning uses neural networks that learn features automatically (A). Generative AI uses deep learning to create new data from what it learned in training (C).

text: Consider the realm of Large Language Models (LLMs). Which of the following options BEST explains why context window limitations affect LLM’s text processing capabilities?

options.text: Because context windows restrict temporal processing sequences, preventing LLMs from maintaining chronological consistency across extended text analysis.
Because context windows prevent cross-referencing capabilities, limiting LLMs’ ability to connect information across different document sources simultaneously.
Because context windows force LLMs to discard earlier information, which may contain relevant details needed for understanding later content.
Because context windows constrain parsing granularity levels, restricting LLMs from adjusting between character-level and document-level analysis approaches.

explanation: An LLM can only process a limited number of tokens at once. When input or conversation exceeds the context window, earlier content is dropped or ignored, so details needed later may be lost. The other options describe invented constraints (temporal sequencing, cross-referencing, parsing granularity).

text: Which of the following statements BEST describes tokenization in processing text for LLMs?

options.text: Tokenization converts tokens into high-dimensional vectors to capture their meaning.
Tokenization creates the building blocks used to understand and generate text.
Tokenization generates contextually appropriate responses using neural networks.
Tokenization predicts the next token in a sequence based on learned relationships.

explanation: Tokenization splits text into tokens, the basic units the LLM works with to understand and generate text. Converting tokens to vectors is embedding; producing responses and predicting the next token are what the model does after tokenization.

text:
In the context of software testing, which of the following statements (i-v) about foundation, instruction-tuned, and reasoning LLMs are CORRECT?

i. Foundation LLMs excel at generating test cases from high-level requirements without structured input.

ii. Reasoning LLMs excel at creating test scripts that strictly follow predefined organizational templates.

iii. Instruction-tuned LLMs excel at autonomously prioritizing test execution based on real-time user feedback.

iv. Reasoning LLMs excel at synthesizing data from defect reports to detect trends and prioritize test efforts.

v. Instruction-tuned LLMs excel at generating test cases that adhere to Gherkin language syntax.

options.text: i, ii, and iii
ii, iii, and iv
i, ii, and v
iv, and v

explanation: Only iv and v are correct: reasoning LLMs suit multi-step analysis such as synthesizing defect reports into trends, and instruction-tuned LLMs follow instructions and formats such as Gherkin. Foundation LLMs need structured prompting rather than excelling with unstructured input (i), reasoning LLMs are not specialised in strict template following (ii), and no LLM autonomously prioritizes execution from real-time user feedback by itself (iii).

text: Which of the following statements BEST describes the relation between multimodal LLMs and vision-language models?

options.text: Multimodal LLMs are a subset of vision-language models designed to handle diverse inputs.
Vision-language models are a subset of multimodal LLMs focusing on visual and textual data.
Vision-language models are unrelated to multimodal LLMs and focus only on the user interface.
Multimodal LLMs and vision-language models are interchangeable terms.

explanation: Multimodal LLMs handle several input types (text, images, audio, ...). Vision-language models are the subset that combines visual and textual data, so VLMs are a subset of multimodal LLMs, not the reverse, and the terms are not interchangeable.

text: Which TWO of the following options represent key capabilities of LLMs in test tasks?

options.text: Identifying ambiguities and inconsistencies in requirements.
Generating complete application code for deployment.
Automating the execution of all test scripts without human intervention.
Performing exploratory testing on software applications.
Creating diverse test data with various combinations and boundary values.

explanation: LLMs are good at spotting ambiguities and inconsistencies in requirements and at generating varied test data including boundary values. They do not replace humans for generating deployable application code, executing all scripts unattended, or performing exploratory testing.

text: Which of the following statements BEST explains the difference between AI chatbots and LLM-powered testing applications in the context of software testing?

options.text: AI chatbots are more suited for specific test tasks, while LLM-powered testing applications focus on ad hoc interactions.
Both AI chatbots and LLM-powered testing applications are designed to perform identical tasks without any configuration differences.
LLM-powered testing applications rely on conversational prompts, while AI chatbots require integration into test tools and test processes.
AI chatbots offer conversational interfaces for ad hoc test tasks, while LLM-powered testing applications provide customized solutions for specific test tasks.

explanation: AI chatbots offer a conversational interface for ad hoc test tasks. LLM-powered testing applications are customised, integrated solutions built for specific test tasks (often with fixed prompts and workflow integration). Options a and c swap or distort the roles.

text: How does Generative AI primarily differ from traditional Machine Learning (ML) or Symbolic AI in a testing context?

options.text: Traditional ML can generate new test artifacts, whereas GenAI only executes deterministic check scripts.
Symbolic AI relies on pre-programmed rules, while GenAI models can synthesize new text, test cases, and scripts based on learned patterns and probabilistic weights.
Traditional ML requires zero training data, while GenAI requires explicit logical rules.
GenAI guarantees 100% deterministic output for identical inputs every time.

explanation: Generative AI uses neural network architectures to produce novel content (like test charters or scripts) probabilistically, contrasting with rule-based symbolic AI or predictive/classification ML models.

text: A tester sends a requirements document longer than the model’s context window. What is the most appropriate response?

options.text: Assume the model can recall omitted text
Split or retrieve relevant sections and preserve necessary context
Increase temperature to enlarge the context window
Fine-tune on a single prompt

explanation: Context windows limit the amount of text processed at once; chunking and retrieval can supply relevant context.

text: Which operation converts text into smaller units before it is processed by an LLM?

options.text: Embedding retrieval
Tokenization
Fine-tuning
Data poisoning

explanation: Tokenization divides text into tokens used by the language model.

text: A QA team needs an LLM to consistently follow a detailed output template. Which model category is particularly suitable?

options.text: A symbolic expert system
An instruction-tuned LLM
A relational database
A clustering algorithm

explanation: Instruction-tuned models are optimized to follow explicit user instructions and formats.

text: A tester wants to compare a screenshot against a written UI requirement. What capability is most directly relevant?

options.text: A text-only classifier
A vision-language model
A database index
A random seed

explanation: Vision-language models can process image and text inputs together.

text: What is a reasonable use of GenAI during requirements analysis?

options.text: Guarantee requirements are defect-free
Identify potential ambiguity for human review
Replace stakeholder approval
Automatically prove system correctness

explanation: LLMs can flag possible ambiguities; testers still validate findings.

text: A team needs repeatable integration of AI-generated test cases into its test management workflow. Which approach fits best?

options.text: Only informal chatbot conversations
An LLM-powered testing application integrated with existing tools
Manual copy-paste without review
Removing all test management tools

explanation: An integrated application can support a defined repeatable workflow.

text: Which of the following uses deep learning techniques to create new content?

options.text: Symbolic AI
Classical machine learning
Deep learning
Generative AI

explanation: Generative AI uses deep learning techniques to create new data by learning and mimicking patterns from the training data.

text: You have used the same prompt multiple times, but you have received different responses from the LLM. Why is this happening?

options.text: Because the prompt is incorrect
Because LLMs have non-deterministic behavior
Because the training data was faulty
Because LLMs are trained to always vary the response

explanation: LLMs exhibit non-deterministic behavior due to the probabilistic nature of their inference mechanisms.

text: How is tokenization related to embeddings?

options.text: Tokens are a numeric representation of how a given word is embedded into the model
Tokens represent characters, subwords, or words, and embeddings capture the semantic, syntactic, and contextual relationship of the tokens
Embeddings describe the text component in such a way that it can be tokenized for use within the model
Embeddings identify the non-deterministic behavior of a word component, which is then used to determine the positioning of its token using a vector to represent its position

explanation: Tokenization splits text into tokens (characters, subwords or words); embeddings are vector representations that capture the semantic, syntactic and contextual relationships between those tokens.

text: You need an LLM that will help with decision-making based on a process similar to human logic. Which type of LLM should you use?

options.text: Foundation LLM
Instruction-tuned LLM
Reasoning LLM
Ad-hoc LLM

explanation: A reasoning LLM is trained specifically to emulate human-like, step-by-step reasoning responses.

text: Which of the following is an advantage of using an LLM augmented with vision-language models for developing test cases?

options.text: There is no advantage because this type of model is used primarily for military applications
It can create test cases that can include text and visual cues
It can edit images much faster and more accurately than a human
It can generate executable code from wireframes and screenshots

explanation: It can create test cases that include both textual data and visual cues, which increases overall test coverage.

text: You have created test automation that will be used to test driver's license applications. There is a huge amount of data available for this testing, but it will take too long to test with all of that data. How can an LLM help with this problem?

options.text: It can create new synthetic data that will protect private information
It can take the existing data and augment that with data that is missing according to the data rules
It can take the existing data and break it into smaller sets that will contain interesting variances
It can delete data that is duplicated and replace it with new data

explanation: The LLM can analyze the existing data and break it into smaller sets that still contain representative and interesting variances.

text: Your organization is developing a test management tool that will use AI to generate, classify, and store test cases based on requirements, general testing knowledge, and previous issues found. Which of the following interaction models would be best to use?

options.text: Chatbots talking to the LLM
Chatbots talking to other chatbots that have been trained on your system
APIs of the LLM to allow the test task information to pass into and out of the LLM
APIs of the LLM to pass the test case information into the LLM to be stored there

explanation: Using the LLM APIs allows maximum use of the LLM by passing the necessary data to and from it. D is wrong because test cases would be stored in the test management system, not in the LLM. A and B are wrong because chatbots are not the most efficient or flexible means of access.

text: Which statement BEST describes a small language model (SLM)?

options.text: A model that cannot be fine-tuned and can only be used in zero-shot mode.
A compact model with fewer parameters that can be fine-tuned to deliver focused task performance with less computational overhead than an LLM.
An LLM variant that always has a larger context window than standard LLMs.
A rule-based symbolic system built for a single test task.

explanation: SLMs are compact models with fewer parameters, designed for lightweight and focused GenAI solutions. Fine-tuning an SLM can reach high task performance without the computational overhead of an LLM (4.2.1). The other options contradict this.

text: A team has two tasks: (1) reformat defect reports into a fixed organizational template; (2) derive a test execution order from risk levels and dependencies between tests. Which model choice is MOST appropriate?

options.text: Task 1: instruction-tuned LLM; Task 2: reasoning LLM.
A foundation LLM for both tasks.
Task 1: foundation LLM; Task 2: instruction-tuned LLM.
Task 1: reasoning LLM; Task 2: instruction-tuned LLM.

explanation: Instruction-tuned LLMs are optimized for task adherence and instruction following (e.g. templates). Reasoning LLMs target multi-step problem solving and suit multi-criteria tasks such as prioritization with dependencies. Foundation models typically need further adaptation.

text: A multimodal LLM receives a GUI screenshot together with a user story. Which statement BEST describes how the screenshot is processed?

options.text: It is converted to text by OCR only, and the image itself is discarded.
It is converted into embeddings by a vision-language model and processed together with the text in the transformer.
It is handled by a separate rule engine, and the results are merged by the tester.
It must first be converted into test scripts before the LLM can use it.

explanation: In multimodal LLMs tokenization is adapted per modality: images are converted into embeddings using vision-language models before being processed in the transformer model.
